findings.claim: mcq-26 is planned as a cross-topic transaction trace and is now SQLite-executed (md method table). The topics it draws on are taught: transactions-and-acid and tables-keys-and-relationships. One general difference between PostgreSQL and SQLite matters for any SQLite-validated transaction item: after an error, PostgreSQL aborts the whole transaction, while SQLite undoes only the failed statement. So a SQLite run is a valid check only when the item's committed state is the same under both behaviours.
findings.recommendation: Confirm privately that mcq-26's committed state is the same under PostgreSQL's whole-transaction abort and SQLite's statement-level undo. If it is not, or cannot be confirmed, treat the item as docs-only and include it in the Open item 4 PostgreSQL run. Record only the value-free outcome of that check in the repository.
